title: Descent of bounded finitely presented module families
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, R:I → CommRingCat a diagram of Noetherian rings, c a limit cone of its spectra with affine apex, i∈I, and f:Xi → Spec(Ri) a locally finitely presented qcqs morphism [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Write X for its base change to c.pt [def-pc-base-change]. For a family M_n of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules on X [pqf-def-coherent], zero outside [a,b], there exist j≥i and finitely presented quasi-coherent modules F_n on Xj, zero outside [a,b], whose limit pullbacks are isomorphic to M_n for every integer n. No maps are part of the statement.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of finitePresentation_module_map_descent separately to each term. Use Finset.exists_le on insert i ((Finset.Icc a b).image stages) to find a common stage k; the given i supplies Nonempty I. For degrees inside the interval define F_n as the tensor pullback of the descended model to k, and for all remaining degrees define it as the free sheaf on PEmpty.

The free sheaf on PEmpty is zero: its identity equals zero by Sigma.hom_ext and elimination of an empty generator. Its standard free generating sections form finite locally free data, since the generator set is empty and finite; finite local freeness implies finite presentation. The other terms are finitely presented by isFinitePresentation_tensorPullback. Finite presentation implies quasicoherence in Mathlib. This proves every support and finiteness assertion.

At each supported degree, tensorPullbackCompositionIso identifies the pullback of the transported model with the original limit pullback; compose this with its chosen term isomorphism. The equality of composite base-change morphisms follows by baseChangeMap_comp and the cone equation. Outside the interval, tensor pullback is left adjoint, hence preserves zero morphisms and zero objects; use the unique isomorphism to the given zero M_n. Zero preservation uses nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction from the module-pullback node, not the separate canonical-unit adjunction theorem.

proof_origin.note: P3 complete Lean proof from the existing one-object descent theorem, finite directed upper bounds, and tensor pullback composition. The zero family is constructed as a free sheaf with empty generator set.

mathlib_searches.query: A bounded family of finitely presented quasicoherent sheaves descends to a stage of a directed limit of schemes
A finite family of finitely presented quasicoherent modules and maps descends along a directed affine inverse limit
mathlib_searches.results: Eight sheaf finite-presentation definitions and instances; no geometric family descent theorem.
Directed.finset_le supplies a common stage only; no family or sheaf-map descent theorem.

Affine graded scalar extension descent exists but assumes affine module categories, whereas Xi need not be affine. No scheme-module version; existing finitePresentation_module_map_descent supplies the one-object and one-map primitives.

lean.statement:
theorem bounded_graded_family_descent
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ k : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj k)]
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (M : ℤ → (pullback f (c.π.app (op i))).Modules)
    (a b : ℤ) (hM_zero : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (M n))
    (hM_fp : ∀ n : ℤ, (M n).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hM_qc : ∀ n : ℤ, (M n).IsQuasicoherent) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
      (F : ℤ → (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).Modules),
      (∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (F n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (F n).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (F n).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      Nonempty (∀ n : ℤ,
          (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
            (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
            (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
            (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).obj (F n) ≅ M n)
